recent_articles.title: Centre tells Supreme Court it will bring back persons allegedly ‘pushed’ to Bangladesh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Centre** informed the **Supreme Court of India** that it will repatriate individuals deported to Bangladesh and verify their citizenship claims upon return. The government's decision comes in response to a September 2025 order from the Calcutta High Court that overturned the deportation of Sunali Khatun and others, deeming it illegal.  The court has scheduled a hearing for July.

recent_articles.title: Bengali actors face heat after power shift to BJP; FIR filed over 2021 social media posts linked to post-poll violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Parambrata Chatterjee**, a Bengali actor, announced he had to align with the **Trinamool Congress** after the recent West Bengal Assembly election results.  He stated this decision was made for his one-year-old son, prompting strong reactions from social media users and fellow actors. **Keya Ghosh**, a BJP leader, responded by criticizing Chatterjee's compromise and highlighting the unwavering support of many BJP supporters in the state.

recent_articles.title: West Asia crisis hurting Indian tea exporters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Indian Tea Association (ITA)** officials reported that the West Asia conflict has significantly impacted tea exports, with 87% of India's total exports concentrated in countries around the Gulf of Persia and the Gulf of Oman. The conflict, which began in February, has led to declining export volumes between January and March compared to 2025, as well as increased freight rates and shipping costs. **Dinesh Bihani**, secretary of the Guwahati Tea Auction Buyers’ Association, stated that the economic uncertainty in West Asia is causing importers to be cautious about buying tea, leading to softer demand and price pressure on both domestic and international markets.  The industry remains hopeful for a recovery in trade flows and consumption once stability returns.

recent_articles.title: From rallies to reels: political catchphrases turn dance anthems in Kolkata - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A new genre of political techno remixes has emerged in Kolkata, using catchy hooks and meme-friendly punchlines to criticize politicians. The trend began with songs like "Khela Hobe" and continues with remixed versions of "Hamba Hamba", "Mach Chor", and "File Chor". These songs often target specific individuals or parties, gaining popularity through social media platforms like Instagram and YouTube Shorts.  The use of crude humor and satirical lyrics reflects a culture of insult-flinging on social media while also expressing anger towards political leaders who abuse power.

recent_articles.title: Bangladesh-China talks underway for Tarique Rahman’s first foreign visit - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tarique Rahman**, Bangladesh's new Prime Minister, is in talks with **China** to visit the country in late June.  The **Chinese** government is keen on welcoming him for his first foreign trip since taking office in February. The planned visit will include high-level meetings between **Rahman** and top Chinese leaders, including President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Li Keqiang.

recent_articles.title: Calcutta High Court asks Bengal government to decide on exemption in animal slaughter rules for Eid ul-Adha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Calcutta High Court** directed the **West Bengal government** to decide on an exemption request for animal slaughter during Eid al-Adha, citing Section 12 of the West Bengal Animal Slaughter Control Act, 1950. The court emphasized that a decision should be made within 24 hours of receiving the order, considering the potential festival dates of May 27 or 28.  The petitioners argued for an exemption based on religious practices and claimed the Act's provisions allow for such relaxation, while opposing lawyers maintained that the notification issued on May 13th was in accordance with existing laws and previous court rulings. The court also urged the state to assess its capacity to issue necessary certificates and ensure proper infrastructure for animal slaughter.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal government to detect, delete and deport illegal infiltrators, says CM Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced a new policy of "detect, delete, and deport" for illegal infiltrators.  He stated that the state police will arrest those not covered under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and hand them over to the **Border Security Force (BSF)** for deportation. The announcement was made during an event where land was handed over to the BSF for border fencing along 27 km of the India-Bangladesh border.  The Chief Minister also emphasized the revival of district-level coordination mechanisms between the BSF, state police, and administration in bordering areas.

recent_articles.title: After State-run schools, Vande Mataram now compulsory in all Bengal madrasas - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education** has mandated the singing of "Vande Mataram" during assembly prayers in all government, aided, and recognized madrasas across the state. The order, issued by the Director of Madrasa Education, states that this is effective immediately and supersedes previous practices.  This decision follows a similar mandate for state-run schools announced earlier in May.

recent_articles.title: Athlete Swapna Barman becomes victim of poll violence, house attacked - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Swapna Barman**, an Asian Games gold medalist and Trinamool Congress candidate, reported that her property was set on fire by unidentified individuals after the 2026 West Bengal Assembly election. **Abhishek Banerjee**, a Trinamool Congress general secretary, accused **BJP** supporters of the arson attack and claimed it reflects the "violence, intimidation, and fear" directed at Trinamool supporters.  The **BJP** government has denied these allegations while **Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari** pledged to ensure the safety of those displaced by violence.

recent_articles.title: Adhikari aide killing: CBI conducts searches at multiple locations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The CBI** conducted searches at multiple locations in connection with the murder of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandrakant Rath. The agency took over the investigation from the **West Bengal Police**, forming a seven-member special investigation team under a DIG of Special Crime from Delhi.  Rath was shot dead on May 6th, two days after the West Bengal Assembly election results were declared. Three individuals have been arrested in connection with the case, while police believe at least eight people were involved.

recent_articles.title: One month of Samrat Choudhary Government in Bihar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, took office as Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  He has implemented several initiatives focusing on development and combating corruption, including a blueprint for 11 satellite townships across 10 districts. The government also launched the "Police Didi Scheme" to enhance women's safety, established a three-tier public support system, and approved significant funding for education and infrastructure projects. Choudhary has also introduced measures to promote transparency in private schools and prioritize local contractors on civil projects.

recent_articles.title: Will lead to further inflation, growth estimates will be lowered considerably: Congress on fuel hike - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress** criticized the **Modi government** for increasing petrol and diesel prices, claiming it will exacerbate inflation and lower growth estimates. The party's general secretary, **Jairam Ramesh**, stated that despite falling international oil prices for years, domestic prices remained high, leading to consumer exploitation.  Fuel prices were hiked by ₹3 per litre each on Friday (May 15, 2026), marking the first increase in over four years and coming after a period of price freezes. The hike was attributed to rising global crude prices triggered by the West Asia conflict and is expected to impact inflation and growth estimates.

recent_articles.title: BJP MLA Rathindra Bose to be party's candidate for Speaker's post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party** in West Bengal has nominated **Rathindra Bose**, a first-time MLA and chartered accountant, as its candidate for the Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly.  Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari urged opposition parties to unanimously elect him. The elections are scheduled for May 15, 2026.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal government mandates singing Vande Mataram in all State-run schools during morning assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, issued an order mandating the singing of **Vande Mataram** in all state-run schools during school assembly prayers. This order overrides a previous directive requiring schools to sing the state song, **Banglar Mati, Banglar Jol**. The move comes amidst political tensions surrounding the national song's recognition and follows a BJP campaign highlighting alleged neglect by the Trinamool Congress government.

recent_articles.title: One dead, several injured in landslide in Jamuria coal mines in West Bengal; many feared missing - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A landslide at the Kunustoria Padashiya Colliery in West Bengal's Jamuria coal belt on Thursday, May 14, 2026, resulted in one fatality and multiple injuries. **Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL)** workers were trapped inside the collapsed mine after an air blast during blasting operations.  Rescue efforts are ongoing, with injured workers being treated at local hospitals. Local residents and union leaders have demanded fair compensation for the deceased and injured workers.

recent_articles.title: ED arrests Kolkata Police DC Shantanu Sinha Biswas in money laundering case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** officials arrested **Shantanu Sinha Biswas**, Deputy Commissioner of Kolkata Police, on Thursday for his alleged involvement in land grabbing and money laundering linked to businessman **Sona Pappu**.  The arrest follows repeated summons by the ED and a lookout notice issued against him for failing to appear. The investigation is ongoing, with the ED seeking information from the West Bengal Police regarding Biswas' current deployment. This marks the second high-profile arrest by the ED since the change of regime in West Bengal.

recent_articles.title: Mamata dons lawyer’s robe, Calcutta HC directs police to ensure safe return of victims affected by violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, former West Bengal Chief Minister, appeared before the Calcutta High Court on Thursday, May 14, 2026, alleging police inaction during post-election violence.  She claimed that she is unable to file complaints in person and has been forced to lodge them online. The court directed the **West Bengal police** to ensure safe returns for those illegally evicted from their homes or businesses due to post-election violence.  The Trinamool Congress welcomed the intervention, while protests erupted from a section of lawyers who chanted "chor chor" (thief thief) slogans.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal CM gives sanction to CBI to prosecute officials in several scams - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, granted permission to the **CBI** to prosecute officials involved in teacher's recruitment, municipality recruitment, and cooperative scams.  He stated that these investigations were previously withheld by the previous Trinamool Congress government due to corruption concerns. The move is part of a "zero tolerance" policy against corruption adopted by his BJP-led administration.  The Chief Minister also lifted a ban on potato sales to other states, citing a bumper crop and falling prices.

recent_articles.title: Berger Paints shares soar over 9% after Q4 net profit jumps 27% to Rs 335 crore - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Berger Paints India** reported a 6.1% increase in consolidated revenue for the March quarter, driven by healthy volume growth and favorable product mix. The company's gross margin reached its highest level in three years, aided by lower raw material prices and partial benefits from anti-dumping duty removal on titanium dioxide. Despite this positive performance, **Berger Paints India** saw a 4.6% decline in net profit for the fiscal year due to implementation of new labor codes and a warehouse fire. The company expects staggered price hikes to support gross margins and ongoing cost optimization efforts to maintain operating margins within their guided range.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court to hear ED plea against bail granted to accused in West Bengal coal scam case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** agreed to hear the **Enforcement Directorate’s** (ED) appeal against the grant of anticipatory bail to Anup Majee, accused of leading a coal mining scam in West Bengal. The **ED** claims that Mr. Majee operated with the “active” assistance of several leaders from the **All India Trinamool Congress**.  The court sought Mr. Majee’s response to the agency's plea challenging a June 2025 order granting him bail in a money laundering case registered in 2020.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool’s land policy delayed West Bengal border fencing: MHA’s 2023 affidavit in Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** stated in a Supreme Court affidavit that the former **Trinamool Congress** government's slow and complex Direct Land Purchase Policy hindered land acquisition for border fencing along the Bangladesh border. The **BJP** government, after assuming power, announced plans to transfer land to the **Border Security Force (BSF)** within 45 days.  The West Bengal government has handed over 78 km of border land to the BSF in the past three years, while 121 km remains to be transferred. The Calcutta High Court is currently reviewing the applicability and feasibility of acquiring land using Section 40 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act (LARR Act), 2013.

recent_articles.title: ‘Bangla Pokkho’ founder Garga Chatterjee arrested for spreading EVM misinformation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Garga Chatterjee**, founder of the pro-Bengali advocacy organization **Bangla Pokkho**, was arrested by the **Kolkata Police** on Tuesday for allegedly spreading misinformation about EVM manipulation during the recent West Bengal Assembly elections. The arrest followed a complaint filed by the District Election Officer of Kolkata North and comes after Mr. Chatterjee's previous arrest in 2022 for alleged community-based hate speech.  Former Trinamool Congress Minister **Sujit Bose** was also sent to 10-day ED custody on Tuesday, accused of illegally recommending candidates for South Dum Dum Municipality positions in exchange for financial benefits. Newly appointed West Bengal Sports Minister **Nisith Pramanik** has requested the file related to the Lionel Messi event in Kolkata and plans to take action if necessary.

recent_articles.title: Election results 2026: Why welfare policies aren't winning polls in India like it used to
recent_articles.rephrased_article: India's welfare politics, once a key electoral tool, is facing challenges. While cash transfers and subsidized services have become the norm across parties, recent state elections suggest that extensive welfare delivery alone is no longer enough to secure incumbency.  **Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress**, for example, lost power in West Bengal despite its women-centric welfare schemes. **The Bharatiya Janata Party** has capitalized on expanding welfare architecture, including women's self-help groups and administrative efficiency, while voters are increasingly demanding more than just welfare benefits.  Political scientists argue that this shift signifies a move from the floor of Indian politics to the ceiling, where parties must build coalitions around broader issues like job creation and economic mobility.

recent_articles.title: BJP MLA Tapas Roy sworn in as Pro-tem Speaker of West Bengal Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tapas Roy**, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and MLA from Maniktala, was sworn in as the Pro-Tem Speaker of the West Bengal Assembly on Tuesday, May 12, 2026. **Suvendu Adhikari**, the Chief Minister, attended the ceremony. The oath-taking of other MLAs will be held on Wednesday and Thursday, with the election for Speaker scheduled for Friday.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Will hear Trinamool pleas on victory margins being less than deleted votes in SIR, says Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, leader of the **Trinamool Congress**, appeared before the Supreme Court on Monday, May 11, 2026, to argue that deletions made during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal affected election results.  Senior advocate Kalyan Bandhopadhyay argued that in some seats, the BJP's victory margin was less than the number of votes deleted. The court asked for an application from **Banerjee** to address the issue and promised to seek information about pending appeals from the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court. The Supreme Court also gave the National Investigation Agency two months to complete its probe into the case of seven judicial officers who were gheraoed in Malda on April 1.

recent_articles.title: CM is unsettled by PM’s remarks: BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **BJP** in Karnataka responded to **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah's** criticism of **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, stating that the Prime Minister's speech at a BJP event was within his democratic right. The opposition leader, R. Ashok, argued that the Prime Minister spoke about issues affecting 7 crore Kannadigas and that Siddaramaiah should focus on addressing real concerns in Karnataka rather than being rattled by the remarks.

recent_articles.title: Telangana BJP distances itself from POCSO case against Bandi Sanjay’s son, calls it legal issue - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party** (BJP) in Telangana distanced itself from a POCSO case involving the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Bandi Sanjay Kumar. The state BJP president, N. Ramchander Rao, stated that the party has no connection to the matter and will investigate if any family member is involved.  Rao also addressed allegations of discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted during the recent Assembly elections, claiming it was a clean-up exercise approved by the Election Commission and Supreme Court. He asserted that the SIR aimed to eliminate "bogus" voters and that the results reflected the mandate of genuine voters.

recent_articles.title: Mamata created false narrative on BJP restricting consumption of fish: Dilip Ghosh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dilip Ghosh**, newly sworn-in West Bengal minister, attended a fish festival on Sunday (May 10, 2026) and refuted **Mamata Banerjee's** claims that the BJP would restrict consumption of fish and meat if it won the Assembly polls.  He accused Ms. Banerjee of spreading falsehoods during her campaign and claimed the BJP government will promote self-sufficiency in fish production.  Echoing Mr. Ghosh, **Tapas Roy**, the BJP MLA-elect from Maniktala, stated that the previous TMC regime failed to develop the pisciculture sector.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to chair first Cabinet meeting on May 11, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly elected Chief Minister of **West Bengal**, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday, May 11, at Nabanna.  The meeting will see the allocation of portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in with him on Saturday. The cabinet is expected to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the **Trinamool Congress** regime. Adhikari also plans to meet with top officials from various departments including the police and district magistrates.

recent_articles.title: I-PAC emerges as Trinamool’s fall guy after West Bengal Assembly poll debacle - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** leaders are blaming **I-PAC**, a political consultancy firm, for the party's loss in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections. Senior leader **Kalyan Banerjee** stated that the reliance on **I-PAC** had detrimental effects on the party's organization and that **Abhishek Banerjee's** dependence on the firm was not well received.

recent_articles.title: WB CM Suvendu Adhikari to chair first cabinet meeting today - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly elected Chief Minister of West Bengal, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday (May 11, 2026) at Nabanna. The meeting is expected to allocate portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in alongside him on Saturday (May 9). **Adhikari** also plans to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the previous Trinamool Congress regime and meet with top officials of various departments including police, district magistrates, and the Director General of West Bengal police.

recent_articles.title: Regional, caste calculus in BJP’s West Bengal Cabinet choices - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** appointed five ministers in West Bengal, including **Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari**, to reflect regional and community considerations.  **Dilip Ghosh**, **Agnimitra Paul**, **Ashok Kirtania**, **Kshudiram Tudu**, and **Nisith Pramanik** were sworn in on Saturday (May 9, 2026), representing diverse regions and caste backgrounds. The appointments aim for a balanced representation within the state's legislature.  The BJP now holds a majority in the West Bengal Assembly after winning 207 seats.

recent_articles.title: Fresh overhaul in Suvendu Adhikari administration likely in near future, say officials - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The newly installed **Suvendu Adhikari**-led BJP government in West Bengal is undertaking a sweeping recalibration of its administrative structure, following the unprecedented scale of pre-poll reshuffle by the Election Commission of India.  **Subrata Gupta**, a retired IAS officer who served as Special Roll Observer during the ECI's exercise, was appointed Advisor to the CM, while **Shantanu Bala**, an Additional District Magistrate, was appointed Private Secretary to the CM. The government also reassigned at least 46 WBCS (Executive) officers and transferred 16 officers from the Chief Minister’s Office, signaling a broader realignment of power corridors in Bengal's bureaucracy.  These changes are seen as part of a larger effort to reshape the state apparatus under the new BJP dispensation.

recent_articles.title: Muslim population in India may match that of Indonesia after Census: Kiren Rijiju - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, Union Minister for Minority Affairs, stated that the Muslim population in India is projected to be nearly equal to Indonesia's population after the upcoming Census. He also expressed concerns over the declining Parsi community and dismissed claims of minority threats, emphasizing equality under the Indian Constitution. **Rijiju** highlighted the BJP's victory in West Bengal as a positive development for national security, citing its border proximity to Bangladesh and concerns about illegal migration.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari | The Bengal pivot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, a prominent Trinamool Congress leader, defected to the **BJP** in December 2020 after several senior party members attempted to persuade him to stay.  Adhikari's decision was driven by his ambition to become West Bengal's Chief Minister, an aspiration he felt unattainable within the **Trinamool Congress**. His departure came as a significant blow to the party, especially with the emergence of **Abhishek Banerjee**, Mamata Banerjee's nephew, who had gained prominence in the political landscape.

recent_articles.title: Sheikh Hasina, Awami League congratulate Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sheikh Hasina**, former Prime Minister of Bangladesh, congratulated **Suvendu Adhikari**, the new Chief Minister of West Bengal.  The **Bangladesh Awami League**, banned in Bangladesh, expressed support for Mr. Adhikari and stated that they believe this new chapter will elevate relations between Bangladesh and India. The Awami League was banned following a crackdown on civilians in 2024.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool nominates Sobhandeb as Opposition leader, Firhad as Chief Whip - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** nominated **Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay**, 82, as the Leader of Opposition in the 18th West Bengal Legislative Assembly.  The party will have two deputy leaders of opposition: **Asima Patra** and **Nayna Bandyopadhya**. **Firhad Hakim** has been appointed as the Trinamool Chief Whip. The decision comes after **Mamata Banerjee** lost her seat in the recent Assembly elections.

recent_articles.title: Modi to set the tone for capturing Telangana after Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** is scheduled to visit Telangana on Sunday, marking a significant push by the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** to establish itself as a major electoral force in the state.  Party leaders believe the Prime Minister's address will signal the BJP's intention to capture power in the next Assembly elections and are confident that his popularity will help expand their base.  **N. Ramchander Rao**, **Union Ministers G. Kishan Reddy** and **Bandi Sanjay Kumar** and party workers are anticipating a strong response from the public.

recent_articles.title: People celebrate with sweets and colour as ‘Kanthi’s son’ takes oath in Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kanthi**, the hometown of **Suvendu Adhikari**, celebrated his swearing-in as West Bengal's Chief Minister on Saturday.  His father, **Sisir Adhikari**, a veteran politician, expressed pride in his son's achievement and thanked the people for choosing him. He urged his son to serve the state wholeheartedly and focus on its development.

recent_articles.title: Labour shortage stalls Mananchira-Vellimadukunnu Road widening works - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Road Fund Board** officials cite a labor shortage caused by migrant workers from West Bengal and Assam returning home for the Assembly elections as a major obstacle to widening the Mananchira-Vellimadukunnu Road in Kozhikode. The scarcity of bitumen, also impacting construction progress, has further delayed the project. While some workers have returned, the issue of bitumen supply remains unresolved.

recent_articles.title: Naidu and Pawan congratulate Suvendu Adhikari on taking oath as West Bengal CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **N. Chandrababu Naidu**, **Prime Narendra Modi**, and **K. Pawan Kalyan**  attended the swearing-in ceremony of **Suvendu Adhikari** as Chief Minister of West Bengal in Kolkata. **Naidu** congratulated the new government and expressed his best wishes for its success, while **Pawan Kalyan** highlighted the significance of the BJP's victory in addressing concerns about violence, lawlessness, and national security.

recent_articles.title: Which party governs which State/UT: In maps - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and its allies secured victories in Assam, Puducherry, and West Bengal, while the Congress-led UDF won in Tamil Nadu. **Suvendu Adhikari**, a BJP leader, is set to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal. The results mark a shift in the political landscape with the BJP or the NDA now governing 20 states and 2 Union Territories.
